findings.summary: No machine geometry is drawn on any of the four panels, so a reader cannot see where the plasma sat relative to the wall. draw_wall is handed the artifact's `wall` array, and that array is the flux-grid bounding box rather than the DIII-D limiter: all 132 points lie on the rectangle's boundary (34 distinct R values, 34 distinct Z values, corners at (0.806,-1.664), (2.574,-1.664), (2.574,1.664), (0.806,1.664)). The rendered result is a plain black rectangle inset in each panel (raster x 26-289, y 39-534, aspect 0.532 against the wall's R:Z aspect 0.531), which reads as a plot frame rather than a vessel. The real limiter and the host_boundary_read bounding surface the brief required are absent, and with the axes off and no scale annotation nothing in the image maps a position to R or Z. The record these figures illustrate claims the terminals touch the upper limiter shelf near R=1.65 m, Z=+1.07 m; the figure cannot show that, which is the one comparison the panels exist to support.

The blue contours are drawn in two line styles with no stated meaning, and in this panel the legend describes a style that is not present. Every contour here is dashed: all seven levels are negative (levels -4.199 to -0.630), and matplotlib dashes contours at negative levels by default, which the raster confirms (longest continuous vertical blue run 13 px, a dash length, against 80-115 px solid stretches in the other three panels). The legend offers a single solid blue 'solved flux' entry, so on this panel the key's blue sample has no counterpart in the plotted data and the dashed curves are a visible mark style the key never explains. Across the set (137 and 44 have four of seven levels negative, 144 has six) the solid-to-dashed switch runs through one field, so the style reads as an encoding but carries no meaning a reader can recover.

The two null markers are drawn but never identified, and only one null set is plotted. Each panel carries one filled red triangle and one filled red asterisk in the same #cc0000, with no legend entry, and only the frame-179 caption's prose mentions 'the axis and the admitted saddle' - without saying which mark is which. The captions for frames 44, 144 and 137 do not mention them at all. The brief asked for both null sets, and the EFIT X-point is absent entirely: draw_nulls receives only the solved arm's axis and saddle, so the solved (limited) and reference (diverted) topology cannot be compared at their nulls.

This figure's caption asserts 'the only arm where Newton promotions are accepted', which the run's own record contradicts at the same head: landing.md records frame 146 diverted with 48 attempted and 48 accepted promotions over four trips. The claim was true of the five-frame table it was written beside, before the 146 arm was recovered, and it was not updated when the fragment was revised. A reader who reaches the residual table after the figure meets a different count, and frame 44's caption ('Frame 44, limited seed, terminal residual 0.197.') is a bare residual line that also leaves the encoding unstated. The caption text is not changed by this review.

More than half of each delivered image is empty white space: the data panel occupies x 26-289 of a 535-pixel-wide canvas, the legend ends by y 75, and about 92 percent of every row below the legend is blank. The figure is a portrait panel rendered into the landscape canvas declared in the drawing script (14 x 7.2 in), and bbox_inches='tight' then crops to 535x574 px, so the delivered raster is 27 percent of the 1400-pixel width the house style specifies. This is layout waste rather than a reading defect - the legend text at 14 pt is legible at the delivered size - and it applies to all four panels.
